questions.stem: Why is burning fossil fuels increasing the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?

options.text: Because it releases carbon that was locked away for millions of years back into the atmosphere
Because burning creates new carbon atoms
Because fossil fuels absorb carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide that was removed from the atmosphere millions of years ago and stored in the fuels. This adds extra CO2 to the atmosphere faster than natural processes can remove it.
